postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Defaulting cook_method to 1 selects raw_html for every ordinary post and enables site-wide stored XSS by bypassing the normal cooker.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. Looking at app/models/post.rb, the cook_methods enum is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, which means :regular = 1 and :raw_html = 2 (Enum starts at 1 by default in Discourse). The migration sets default to 1, which corresponds to :regular (the normal cooking method), not :raw_html. The cook method in post.rb shows `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` - only raw_html (value 2) bypasses cooking. Default of 1 means regular cooking is applied, which is correct behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — Feed item HTML is imported into raw_html posts without sanitization, so a compromised feed can execute arbitrary script for forum visitors.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in poll_feed.rb:35, content from RSS feeds is passed to TopicEmbed.import() which creates posts with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]. Looking at post.rb lines 131-133, when cook_method is raw_html, the cook() method returns raw content directly without any processing. The content from feeds (i.e.content from RSS) goes through CGI.unescapeHTML but no HTML sanitization. In topic_embed.rb line 21, the import method creates posts with skip_validations: true and cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], meaning malicious HTML/JavaScript from a compromised feed would be rendered directly to users without sanitization, creating an XSS vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:52 — Host validation occurs only before open follows redirects, so an allowed-host open redirect can drive server-side requests to internal services.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real security concern. In lib/topic_retriever.rb, the invalid_host? method at line 14-18 only validates the initial URL's host against SiteSetting.embeddable_host. However, in fetch_http (line 49-53), TopicEmbed.import_remote is called which uses open(url).read (seen in app/models/topic_embed.rb line 47). Ruby's open-uri follows HTTP redirects by default, so if an allowed host (e.g., eviltrout.com) has an open redirect vulnerability, an attacker could craft a URL that passes the host validation but redirects to internal services (SSRF). The host validation happens before the HTTP request, not after following redirects.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:40 — Every distinct missing embed URL runs the entire feed poll, allowing unique-path requests to amplify into repeated feed downloads and full import scans.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a performance/DoS issue in lib/topic_retriever.rb. Looking at lines 35-42 in perform_retrieve(), when feed_polling_enabled is true, every unique embed_url that doesn't exist in TopicEmbed will trigger Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}). This polls the entire RSS feed and processes all items. An attacker could send requests with many different embed_url paths (e.g., /page1, /page2, etc.) and each unique URL would bypass the 60-second throttle (since throttle is per-URL) and trigger a full feed poll. This is a real amplification vulnerability where N unique URL requests cause N full feed downloads and import scans.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — One malformed feed item aborts the remaining import loop while retries are disabled, delaying every later item until the next hourly poll.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the job has `sidekiq_options retry: false` (line 12) and the `poll_feed` method iterates through `rss.items.each` (line 31-36). If any item processing fails (e.g., malformed content, invalid URL, encoding issues), the exception will propagate and abort the entire loop since there's no error handling around individual items. With retries disabled, this means all subsequent items won't be processed until the next hourly poll. This is a real bug - a single bad feed item can block processing of all remaining items.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — The public embed snippet concatenates `discourseUrl` without normalizing a trailing slash, so a normal origin value such as `https://forum.example.com` produces an invalid `/embed/best` URL and breaks the integration.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/assets/javascripts/embed.js line 7: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + encodeURIComponent(discourseEmbedUrl);`. The code concatenates discourseUrl directly with 'embed/best'. If discourseUrl is 'https://forum.example.com' (without trailing slash), the result would be 'https://forum.example.comembed/best?...' which is invalid. If it has a trailing slash like 'https://forum.example.com/', it would work correctly. This is a real bug where the URL construction doesn't handle the presence/absence of a trailing slash in discourseUrl.

This is a documented CLI option (`-c`) that existing users may depend on. Removing it without deprecation notice breaks backward compatibility - existing scripts using `--category` or `-c` will fail. The finding correctly identifies this as a breaking change to the CLI contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:57 — Protocol-relative links such as //cdn.example.com/a are rewritten as paths on the article host, breaking imported links and images.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the absolutize_urls method in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 51-68, the code checks `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` and `if src.present? && src.start_with?('/')`. Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/a` do start with '/', so they would match this condition and be incorrectly rewritten to `{prefix}//cdn.example.com/a` (e.g., `http://eviltrout.com//cdn.example.com/a`), breaking the link. This is a real bug in the URL handling logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:54 — Path-relative URLs such as images/a.png and ../article are left relative to Discourse instead of being resolved against the source article URL.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the absolutize_urls method in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 52-70, the code only handles URLs that start with '/' (absolute paths). The condition `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` and `if src.present? && src.start_with?('/')` means that relative URLs like 'images/a.png' or '../article' (which don't start with '/') will not be converted to absolute URLs. These relative URLs would remain relative to Discourse's domain instead of being resolved against the source article URL. This is a real bug in the URL handling logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:14 — Host validation compares DNS names case-sensitively, so a valid embed URL whose hostname casing differs from the configured host is rejected.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb:14, the code compares `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`. DNS hostnames are case-insensitive per RFC standards, but Ruby string comparison is case-sensitive. If the configured embeddable_host is 'eviltrout.com' but a URL comes in as 'http://EvilTrout.com/page', the comparison would fail even though they refer to the same host. This is a real bug in the validation logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — force: true` can silently drop an existing `topic_embeds` table and all of its data when this migration runs or is retried.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` in db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb. The `force: true` option will drop the table if it already exists before creating it, which could cause data loss if the migration is re-run or if a table with that name already exists. This is a real defect - migrations should not use `force: true` as it can silently destroy data. The same pattern is also visible in db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb which was modified to add `force: true`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — Changing this historical migration to `force: true` makes any future execution silently drop and recreate `top_topics`, destroying accumulated ranking data.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a change to db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb at line 4, changing from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. The `force: true` option in Rails migrations causes the table to be dropped if it exists before creating it. For a historical migration that may have already run in production, adding `force: true` means if the migration is ever re-run (e.g., during database reset or in certain edge cases), it would silently drop the existing top_topics table and all its data. This is a real data loss risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — import mutates its caller-owned contents string in place, creating a hidden coupling that can contaminate reuse or retries

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in app/models/topic_embed.rb line 13, the import method mutates the contents parameter with `contents << "\n<hr>\n<small>..."`. This modifies the caller's string in place using `<<` operator. While this is a real code smell that could cause issues if the caller reuses the contents variable, it's not strictly a bug since the current callers (poll_feed.rb and import_remote) don't appear to reuse the contents after calling import. It's a valid architectural concern about hidden coupling and potential for future bugs, but not a current defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — TopicRetriever directly instantiates and executes a scheduled job, coupling reusable retrieval logic to the job wrapper instead of a shared feed-import service

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in lib/topic_retriever.rb:41, the code directly instantiates and executes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) within the perform_retrieve method. This is a valid architectural concern - the TopicRetriever class is tightly coupled to the job wrapper rather than extracting the feed polling logic into a reusable service. However, this is a design/architecture concern rather than a bug - the code will function correctly. The finding is grounded in actual diff code at the specified location.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — feed_key and its digest dependency are dead code because no path reads the method

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the `feed_key` method defined at line 20-22 in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb is never called anywhere in the diff. The method computes a SHA1 digest of the feed URL but is not used by `poll_feed` or any other code shown. This appears to be dead code that was likely intended for caching/tracking purposes but was never integrated. While not a bug (the code still functions), it's a legitimate code quality issue - unused code that adds confusion and maintenance burden.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1 — The new email/sender dependency is unused and adds an unrelated load-time coupling to the retrieval job

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb in the diff, line 1 shows `require_dependency 'email/sender'`. While this dependency does appear unused in the file (the file only uses TopicRetriever), this is a minor code hygiene issue, not a bug or important non-bug. It's essentially a style/cleanup nit - an unused require doesn't cause any functional problems, it just adds a small unnecessary load. The finding is technically accurate but falls into the category of pure style/format nit that doesn't warrant action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Throttling occurs only inside the worker, so every cache miss or loading-page refresh still enqueues a redundant job and can exhaust the queue under embed traffic.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in embed_controller.rb line 15, when topic_id is nil, it enqueues a job with `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. The throttling logic is in TopicRetriever (lib/topic_retriever.rb) which checks `retrieved_recently?` using Redis setnx. However, the job is enqueued BEFORE any throttling check happens - the throttling only occurs when the job executes. This means every request to the embed endpoint with a cache miss will enqueue a new job, even if the same URL was just requested. Under high traffic to the same embed URL, this could flood the job queue with redundant jobs before the first one completes and sets the Redis key. The finding correctly identifies that throttling happens inside the worker, not at the controller level where the job is enqueued.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — The remote article body is read fully with no size bound before parsing, so an oversized response can consume unbounded worker memory.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48, the code does `open(url).read` which reads the entire remote response into memory without any size limit. This is called in `import_remote` method. An attacker could provide a URL that returns an extremely large response, causing unbounded memory consumption on the worker. This is a real security/resource exhaustion vulnerability introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — Every poll walks the entire feed and performs per-item database import lookups, so feed size drives unbounded memory and query work instead of a capped batch.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that poll_feed.rb iterates over all items in the RSS feed (rss.items.each) and calls TopicEmbed.import for each one, which performs database operations. However, this is not a bug per se - it's a design concern about scalability. The code does work correctly, but for very large feeds it could be inefficient. The import method does check for existing embeds (TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first) which provides some optimization, but the concern about unbounded iteration is valid. This is an architectural/scope concern rather than a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — Acquiring the throttle before retrieval makes Sidekiq retries exit successfully after a transient fetch failure, so the failed import is not retried.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb, the `retrieved_recently?` method sets a Redis key with 60-second expiry BEFORE `perform_retrieve` is called. The flow in `retrieve` is: check `invalid_host?`, then check `retrieved_recently?` (which sets the throttle), then call `perform_retrieve`. If `perform_retrieve` fails (e.g., network error during `fetch_http` or `TopicEmbed.import_remote`), the throttle key is already set, so any Sidekiq retry within 60 seconds will see `retrieved_recently?` return true and exit without retrying the actual retrieval. This is a real bug where transient failures won't be retried properly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:12 — Disabling retries for the whole feed means one transient fetch, parse, or item-import exception aborts the batch and delays all remaining imports until a later schedule.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that `sidekiq_options retry: false` at line 12 of poll_feed.rb means if any exception occurs during feed polling (network error, parse error, or individual item import failure), the entire job fails without retry. Looking at the `poll_feed` method, it iterates through `rss.items.each` and calls `TopicEmbed.import` for each item - if any single item fails, the remaining items won't be processed until the next hourly schedule. This is a legitimate architectural concern about error handling in the new code, though it's not a bug per se since the behavior is intentional (just potentially suboptimal for resilience).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Every concurrent cache miss enqueues a retrieval job before deduplication occurs inside the worker, allowing a traffic burst to flood the shared job queue.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the embed_controller.rb code at line 15, when topic_id is nil, it enqueues a job with `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. The TopicRetriever class does have throttling via `retrieved_recently?` which uses Redis setnx with a 60-second expiry, but this throttling happens INSIDE the job worker (in `perform_retrieve`), not before the job is enqueued. This means if multiple requests come in simultaneously for the same embed_url before any job starts processing, multiple jobs will be enqueued to the queue. The deduplication only prevents the actual HTTP fetch, but the jobs are still queued. This is a valid concern about queue flooding during traffic bursts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Imported RSS content is persisted as raw HTML without sanitization, allowing a malicious or compromised feed to execute stored XSS for topic viewers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in topic_embed.rb line 22, PostCreator is called with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and in post.rb lines 131-133, when cook_method is raw_html, the cook method returns `raw` directly without any processing. The RSS content from poll_feed.rb is passed through CGI.unescapeHTML but no HTML sanitization is applied. The content is then rendered in best.html.erb using `raw post.cooked`, which outputs unescaped HTML. This creates a stored XSS vulnerability where malicious content in an RSS feed could execute JavaScript when users view the embedded topic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — The server fetch follows an allowed host without revalidating redirect destinations or resolved private addresses, enabling SSRF through an open redirect or DNS rebinding.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real SSRF vulnerability in TopicEmbed.import_remote at line 48, which uses `open(url).read` to fetch content from user-controlled URLs. The code only validates the host in TopicRetriever.invalid_host? before calling perform_retrieve, but import_remote itself has no validation. Additionally, even when called through TopicRetriever, the validation only checks the initial URL's host against embeddable_host - it doesn't prevent redirects to internal/private addresses or DNS rebinding attacks. The open() call will follow redirects automatically, allowing an attacker to bypass the host check via an open redirect on the allowed host or DNS rebinding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43 — The no-embed example still expects a synchronous TopicRetriever call even though the controller now enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic, so this new spec fails and never verifies the actual job payload.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the embed_controller.rb shows that when no topic_id is found, it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` (line 14-15). However, the test in spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb at lines 41-47 expects `TopicRetriever.new` to be called directly and `retriever.retrieve` to be invoked synchronously. Since the controller actually enqueues a job rather than calling TopicRetriever directly, this test expectation is incorrect and the test would fail. The test mocks TopicRetriever but the controller never instantiates TopicRetriever directly - it enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic which internally uses TopicRetriever.
